title: ZnS-MgF2 Alternating Dual-Band IR Filter on Daimon-20
scientific_hypothesis: An alternating high-low index dielectric stack with optimized individual layer thicknesses can produce two distinct transmission bands at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm while suppressing transmission at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, using only conventional IR-transparent materials.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory: alternating layers of high and low refractive index create constructive interference in passbands and destructive interference in stopbands. For dual-band operation, the layer thicknesses must be tuned so that multiple harmonic orders of the stack align with both target wavelengths. ZnS provides high index (~2.2-2.4 in mid-IR), MgF2 provides low index (~1.3-1.4 in mid-IR), giving sufficient index contrast for effective filtering.
proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack: ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2/ZnS/MgF2 on Daimon-20 substrate, air incident
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ZnS and MgF2 are both conventional evaporatable/sputterable IR dielectrics
Daimon-20 substrate is IR-transparent and thermally stable
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance at design wavelength when optical thickness equals λ/4
Recalled knowledge: Dual-band filters require thickness tuning so multiple interference orders align with both passbands
Recalled knowledge: ZnS has refractive index approximately 2.2-2.4 in the 4-5 μm range with low absorption
Recalled knowledge: MgF2 has refractive index approximately 1.3-1.4 in the 4-5 μm range with low absorption
Recalled knowledge: Index contrast of ~0.8-1.0 between high and low layers provides adequate reflectance per interface for IR filtering
expected_advantages: ZnS/MgF2 pair is well-established for IR coatings from recalled practice
22 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
Alternating topology is manufacturable with standard deposition equipment
No metal layers avoids absorption losses in the IR
known_risks: Uncertain whether ZnS and MgF2 remain sufficiently transparent at 5.2 μm - may have absorption edges I cannot recall precisely. Would need to check measured k values in the material registry.
Uncertain about exact refractive index dispersion in the 3.6-5.2 μm range - my recalled values are approximate. The solver will read actual measured data.
Uncertain whether 22 layers is optimal vs 20 or 24 - chose 22 as a middle value from recalled practice but this is not verified.
Uncertain about adhesion between ZnS and MgF2 on Daimon-20 - may require adhesion layers not modeled here.
The quarter-wave starting point may not be optimal for dual-band operation; thickness optimization is essential.
Daimon-20 is one of four CaF2 datasets in the registry; I cannot verify from memory whether this specific dataset covers the full 3.6-5.2 μm range needed.
execution_request_english: Design a 22-layer planar multilayer infrared filter coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. Use alternating ZnS and MgF2 layers starting with ZnS as layer 1. Optimize individual layer thicknesses with bounds 50-1000 nm per layer. Target high transmittance in two passbands: 4150-4350 nm and 4550-4750 nm. Target low transmittance in two stopbands: 3600-4000 nm and 4850-5200 nm. Use coherent thin-film matrix method solver. Evaluate unpolarized light at normal incidence. Maximum 24 layers constraint satisfied with 22 layers. No metal layers used. Materials ZnS and MgF2 are from the guaranteed material catalog. Substrate is CaF2 (Daimon-20).
revision_reason: Repaired material name: replaced ambiguous CaF2 with resolved dataset name Daimon-20 per registry requirement
